senses.definition: A flat-bottomed vessel, of width similar to or greater than its height, used for storing or packing things, or for washing things in.
examples: He bought a tub of lard to roast the potatoes in.

senses.definition: The contents or capacity of such a vessel.
examples: She added a tub of margarine to the stew.

quotes.text: Teach me to love my morning tub, / In waters cold to splash and rub; / O, grant my Turkish towel may flood / Its virtues through my soul and blood.
quotes.reference: 1920, Theodore Sharpe, My Place in the Shade: And Various Verse, page 27:

quotes.text: The rest of the evening we had a fine west wind, which carried us on at near five knots an hour, as much as our lumbering old tub can possibly go.

senses.definition: (automotive) The bare body shell of an automobile (minus the doors, hood, trunk lid, fenders, etc.) which is lowered onto the chassis at the time of assembly, or in the case of modern unibody designed vehicles, is itself a monocoque around which the rest of the vehicle is built.
